bug_semantics: Unauthenticated CRLF injection into the system crontab via GET /crontab. Express decodes URL-encoded %0a/%0d in req.query.env_vars; app.js passes that string unsanitized to crontab.set_crontab, which prefixes the generated crontab file with `${envVars}\n` (originally `env_vars + "\n"`) and then execs `crontab <file>`. Lines after the injected newline are treated as extra cron records, so a caller can install arbitrary scheduled commands through a field intended only for crontab environment assignments (PATH, MAILTO, HOME). Basic auth is optional (BASIC_AUTH_USER/PWD); Docker images bind HOST=0.0.0.0:8000.
flaw_origin: The env_vars sink was first written on 2016-02-14 in 0c6cc5512adf5d252b0cd9aa0b7c4c4131661c43 (GitHub PR #4, single commit by Fantoccini). The immediate parent called set_crontab() with no arguments and had no env_vars identifier anywhere in the tree. That commit added crontab.set_crontab(req.query.env_vars) in app.js and `if (env_vars) { crontab_string = env_vars + "\n"; }` in crontab.js with no KEY=value parsing or newline neutralization. Follow-up 5f52cbcf44bf1515d70ad54233e73c3ddc1fc40b only persisted env.db; the 2026 'Major revamp' ecfe9faa586674dccfa20aab3d95f7e7ab5a48a2 rewrote the same concatenation as `${envVars}\n` and is a refactor, not the BIC.

potential_fix.approach: Reject env_vars content that is not a crontab environment assignment: split on newlines, keep only optional comments and NAME=value lines, drop any line matching a cron schedule (five fields or @reboot/@daily/etc. plus a command). Do not write raw req.query.env_vars into the crontab file. Change GET /crontab to POST so query-string CRLF and CSRF-via-GET cannot install jobs. Keep auth optional only behind an explicit bind/auth warning; default Docker should not expose an unauthenticated crontab writer on 0.0.0.0.
potential_fix.rationale: The injectable primitive is extra crontab records created from decoded newlines in a parameter meant for env assignments. Accepting only KEY=value/comment lines closes the CWE-93 breakout; moving the install endpoint off GET removes the unauthenticated one-request install path described in the advisory.
